summary: Burst of small batched requests in eu-west causing persistent slot attachment failures and throughput degradation
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-13 08:40 UTC, Verbio (dedicated pool in eu-west) reported sudden degradation in sustained throughput for short, low-token batched inference requests. The customer sees increased p50/p95 latency and a steady fall in token-per-second across their reserved capacity. Impact: customer-facing feature degraded with higher error rates and timeouts, affecting revenue-critical flows. Timeline: 08:40 UTC - customer alert; 08:45 UTC - Support triage; 09:05 UTC - SRE engaged; 09:30 UTC - initial mitigation applied (traffic shaping). Environment: Dedicated reserved capacity (dedicated pool id: dp-eu-142), prod, eu-west. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send many small requests (avg 8-32 tokens) across 100 concurrent connections to the customer's reserved endpoint. 2) Observe steady drop in throughput within 5-15 minutes and rising attach errors. 3) Check serving runtime and scheduler logs for "GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT" and batcher slot allocation errors. Observed behavior: - Persistent "GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT" and "slot_alloc_failed: resource busy" in worker logs. - Autoscaler did not provision new GPUs for ~7 minutes during the surge. - NVML warnings and occasional "Device is busy" kernel messages in node logs. - Prefix/KV cache hit rates unchanged, suggesting request pattern (many small, short-lived sessions) is causing slot churn rather than cache misses. Expected behavior: small-request bursts should be absorbed by existing batchers or result in quick autoscale add of capacity with minimal attach failures. Attachments: links to dashboards and sample logs cited in investigation_notes and comments.
comments: 2026-03-13 08:50 UTC — Support (Aisha): Customer reporting degraded throughput and intermittent 503s. Asked for request sample and client SDK version.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC — SRE (Marcus): Observed repeated GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT across three nodes in dp-eu-142. Opening investigation. Slack thread: #support-dedicated-eu (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C09DDED)
2026-03-13 09:35 UTC — Support (Aisha): Applied temporary traffic shaping on customer route to cap concurrency at 40 to reduce attach churn. Customer reported immediate partial improvement.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC — Engineering (Leila Gomez): Identified a scheduler race where many short-lived sessions trigger reattachment logic; filing infra PR to add hysteresis (see PR 879).
2026-03-13 12:45 UTC — Customer (Verbio AI, Tom R.): Confirmed that after shaping we see fewer 503s but throughput is still ~30% below normal during peak. Asked for root cause and ETA for fix.
investigation_notes: Checked autoscaler logs: predictive window did not trigger scale because average queue length metric remained below threshold despite high attach error rate — queue length metric is averaged over 1m and misses short burst signature.

Worker logs sample (node nv1-eu-23): 'ERROR serving_runtime: GPU_ATTACH_TIMEOUT: failed to attach container to GPU after 120s; slot_alloc_failed: resource busy', repeated ~180 times between 08:38-09:12 UTC.
DB of pool allocations shows slot fragmentation: 62% of GPUs had >80% small-slot occupancy (many 1-request slots) leading to inability to coalesce.
Kernel logs: intermittent 'nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses' latency spikes when attach attempts coincide; suggests NVML endpoint saturation under small-stream fanout.
KV cache footprint stable — rules out cache eviction. Batcher logs show many ephemeral batch windows (window < 30ms) which prevents effective batching and results in many tiny GRPC streams.
Hypothesis A: Noisy-tenant effect — other tenants on same dedicated HW (misconfigured or under wrong affinity) are producing many short streams causing slot churn and NVML contention.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler thresholds tuned for sustained queue growth; short, high-frequency attach-floods bypass trigger causing delayed scale and attach backpressure.

Cross-referenced SUP-631210 (tenant-preemptive-eviction) and SUP-742998 (pcie-saturation) for similar symptoms; differences: this incident shows attach-time NVML saturation rather than PCIe throughput saturation.
Collected packet captures from node nv1-eu-23 and attached to ticket. Dashboard slices: 'dp-eu-142 attach_errors', 'nvml_latency_telemetry', 'batcher_window_histogram' linked in confluence runbook.
Temporary mitigation validated: traffic shaping reduced attach churn and reduced attach_error rate by ~60% in 15 minutes. Customer still below normal throughput.

Engineering has prepared a scheduler patch to: a) add short-burst detection and immediate auto-scale override; b) add attach-request rate-limiter per-node to smooth NVML calls. Patch referenced in PR 879.
Follow-up: Add metric 'attach_error_rate' to alerting and reduce autoscaler averaging window from 1m to 10s for dedicated pools marked 'sensitivity: high'.
resolution: Workaround: Applied per-route concurrency cap (40) and temporary tenant shaping which stabilized attach error rate and partially restored throughput. Long-term fix: merged PR 879 to add burst-detection autoscale override and node-level attach-rate limiting; rollout scheduled to eu-west canary 2026-03-15. Postmortem action items: 1) update autoscaler config for dedicated pools (reduce averaging window for attach-sensitive pools). 2) Add attach_error_rate to console dashboards and alerting. 3) Run dedicated stress test simulating many small ephemeral streams to validate mitigations. Related follow-ups assigned: INT-4022 (scheduler instrumentation) and SUP-742998 (monitor pcie/nvml saturation).
